This manuscript develops a coherent framework that combines Bayesian decision theory with optimal-stopping principles to formalize when to act, when to wait, and how to update beliefs as evidence accumulates. The core contribution is an integrated research design that treats prediction, explanation, and governance as joint outputs of a single lifecycle: prior elicitation, likelihood construction, sequential inference, stopping rules with explicit loss functions, and post-decision auditing for robustness and accountability.
